sentences.text: Petitioner has sought for setting aside of the order passed by respondent No.4 only insofar as imposing of condition by the Special Deputy Commissioner while approving the award to the extent of Rs. 67,64,804/- as found at the bottom of the award dated 01.06.2021.

The only legal contention raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that insofar as the proceedings relating to compensation is concerned, when the award was placed for approval, the Special Deputy Commissioner, KIADB, has approved the award only with respect to the amount of Rs.67,64,804/- which is contrary to the calculation as made in the award which amounts to Rs.6,78,45,690/-.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the approving authority has no power to impose condition.

Reliance is placed on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of VIJAYADEVI NAVALKISHORE BHARTIA AND ANOTHER VS. LAND ACQUISITION OFFICER AND ANOTHER - (2003) 5 SCC 83.
3.

entities.text: VIJAYADEVI NAVALKISHORE BHARTIA AND ANOTHER VS. LAND ACQUISITION OFFICER AND ANOTHER - (2003) 5 SCC 83
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is submitted that in terms of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the aforesaid case,
approving authority has no power under the First proviso to Section 11(1) of the Land Acquisition Act (for short 'the Act') to impose any condition and under Section 15-A of the Act, it NC:
2023:KHC:23637 is only the Government to which the proceedings may be referred which has the power to impose any condition.
4.

Sri. P. V. Chandrashekar, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondents 3 and 4, on the other hand would contend that the Apex Court in Paragraph No.11 of the judgment in the case of VIJAYADEVI (Supra) has referred the matter to a larger Bench.

It is further submitted that the Sri. T. R. Srinivasan vs State Of Karnataka on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134243320/
3 power of imposing condition which may have the effect of amending the award could be traced to Sections 12-A and 13A of the Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Heard both sides.
6.

At the outset, it must be noted that the imposition of condition cannot be permitted in light of the law laid down in the case of VIJAYADEVI (supra) and the approving authority may only refer it to the Government in case any further directions are required for the purpose of imposition of condition in terms of the power conferred under Section 15-A of the Act.

In the NC:
2023:KHC:23637 present case, there is no material forthcoming as regards imposition of condition while approving of the award only to Rs.67,64,804/- instead of quantification of the compensation to Rs.6,78,45,690/-.

Reliance to Sections 12-A and 13-A of the Act cannot be pressed into service as the said provisions come into play only in case of clerical or arithmetical mistake and in the absence of material placed by the respondents, is not the contingency that has occurred.
There is also no dispute with respect to the quantification of Rs.6,78,45,690/-.

The only direction as passed previously in W.P.No.8271/2018 is that the matter is referred to determine the nature of kharab while applying its mind to the objections and to proceed to pass a general award.

7. Accordingly, in the absence of any clerical or arithmetical mistake, question of recourse to Sections 12- A and 13-A of the Act will not apply and accordingly, the condition imposed by the Special Deputy Commissioner at the bottom of the award dated 01.06.2021 including the NC:
2023:KHC:23637 approval are set aside.
The award is to be placed before the approving authority.
It is open for the Authority to place it before the Government for appropriate orders if it is of the opinion that conditions are required to be imposed.
Accordingly, petition is disposed off.
